articles.text: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other provision of the Constitution, the person holding the office of President immediately before the commencement of the Constitution shall be the first President under the Constitution and shall be deemed for all purposes to have been elected as the President of the Republic, and shall, subject to the provisions of Article 31, hold office for a period of six years from February 4, 1978. The President shall, notwithstanding the provisions of Article 32, be deemed to have assumed office immediately upon the commencement of the Constitution and shall be entitled thereupon to exercise, perform and discharge all the powers, duties and functions conferred or imposed on, or assigned to, the President by the Constitution or otherwise. The President shall, as soon as possible thereafter at a sitting of Parliament, take and subscribe the oath or make and subscribe the affirmation set out in the Fourth Schedule.

titution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka (d) (i) where immediately before the commencement of Constitution there was a vacancy in the membership of the National State Assembly or where a vacancy in the membership of the first Parliament occurs otherwise than under the provisions of paragraph (b) of this Article, such vacancy shall be filled in the manner provided in sub-paragraph (iii) hereof; (ii) Where during the duration of the First Parliament, a Member ceases, by resignation, expulsion or otherwise, to be a member of the recognized political party to which he belonged upon or after the commencement of the Constitution, the Secretary of such party shall, within two weeks of the date on which such Member so ceased to be a member of such party, communicate, in writing to the Secretary-General of Parliament, the fact and date thereof. The Secretary-General shall, upon receipt of such communication, submit it to the Speaker. Where a Member ceases to be a member of the recognized political party to which he belonged by reason of being expelled from such party, he shall be entitled to apply, within one month of the date of such expulsion by petition in writing, to the Supreme Court for a determination that such by the Second Amendment to the Constitution Sec. 2. expulsion was invalid. In the event o any such application being made, th Registrar of the Supreme Court sha forthwith inform the Secretary-Genera of Parliament in writing, of suc application, every such applicatio shall be heard and determined by no less than three Judges of the Suprem Court who shall, within two months o the making of such application determine whether such expulsion wa valid or not. The Speaker shall, on receiving in th aforesaid manner, a communicatio alleging that a Member has cease to be a member of the recognize political party to which such Membe belonged, appoint a Select Committe consisting of not less than fiv Members of Parliament (one of whom shall be nominated as Chairma thereof) to inquire into, and report t Parliament on, the circumstances i which such Member is alleged to hav resigned from, or to have bee expelled from, or to have otherwis ceased to be a member of, such party and the reasons therefor: Provided, however, that wher such communication alleges that Member has ceased to be a member o the recognized political party to whic he belonged by reason of his bein expelled therefrom, no Selec Committee shall be appointed a titution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka aforesaid until after the expiration of a period of one month from the date of such alleged expulsion, and in any case where such Member has applied to the Supreme Court for a determination that such expulsion was invalid, unless and until the Supreme Court has determined that such expulsion was valid. The provisions of the Parliament (Powers and Privileges) Act shall, mutatis mutandis, apply in relation to proceedings before, and to the privileges, immunities and powers of, a Select Committee appointed as aforesaid and every such Select Committee shall be deemed, for the purposes of that Act, to be duly authorized by an order of Parliament to send for persons, papers and records. After consideration of the report made by a Select Committee appointed as aforesaid, Parliament may, by resolution passed by not less than eighty-five Members voting in its favour, resolve that the Member to whom such report relates, shall cease to be a Member of Parliament. The Speaker shall endorse on every resolution so passed, a certificate in the following form:– “This resolution has been passed by the majority required by Article 161 (d)(ii) of the Constitution”. The seat of such Member shall, wit effect from the date of such certificate become vacant. Every such certificate shall be conclusiv for all purposes and shall not b questioned in any court, and no cour or tribunal shall inquire into pronounce upon or in any manne call in question, the validity of th resolution on which such certificate i endorsed on any ground whatsoever. articles.description: Judges of Supreme Court and High Court to cease to hold office
articles.text: All Judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts established by the Administration of Justic Law, No.44 of 1973, holding office on the day immediately before the commencement of the Constitution shall, on th commencement of the Constitution, cease to hold office. titution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

articles.description: Continuation in office of Judges, public officers and others
articles.text: Subject to the provisions of Article 163 every person who immediately before the commencement of the Constitution - (a) held office in any court or tribunal deemed, by virtue of the provisions of paragraph

clauses.text: of Article 105, to be a court or tribunal created and established by Parliament, (b) was in the service of the Republic, any local authority or any Public Corporation, (c) held office in any local authority or Pub- lic Corporation, or (d) held any appointment under any existing written law, shall continue in such service or hold such office or appointment under the same terms and conditions.

articles.description: Oath or affirmation to be taken or made by public officers and others

clauses.text: Every public officer, judicial officer and every other person as is required by the Constitution to take an oath or make an affirmation on entering upon the duties of his office, every holder of an office required under the existing law to take an official oath and every person in the service of every local authority and of every Public Corporation shall take and subscribe the oath or make and subscribe the affirmation set out in the Fourth Schedule. Any such public officer, judicial officer, person or holder of an office failing to take and subscribe such oath or make and subscribe such affirmation after the commencement of the Constitution on or before such date as may be prescribed by the Prime Minister by Order published in the Gazette shall cease to be in service or hold office.
The Minister in charge of the subject of Public Administration may, in his sole discretion, permit an public officer, judicial officer, person or holder of a office referred to in paragraph

of this Article, to tak the oath or make the affirmation referred to in th paragraph after the prescribed date if he is satisfied that th failure to take the oath or make the affirmation within th time prescribed was occasioned by illness or some oth unavoidable cause. On his taking such oath or making suc affirmation, he shall continue in service or hold office as he had taken such oath or made such affirmation within th time prescribed under paragraph
of this Article.
The President may by Proclamation – (a) exclude the application of the provisions paragraph

of this Article to any catego of public officers, (b) prescribe the persons or categories of perso who may administer such oath or affirmatio in addition to the persons who are empowere under the existing law to administer oaths affirmations.
